newsitem.title: UK: Britons win race claim against Japanese company.
newsitem.headline: Britons win race claim against Japanese company.

text.p: Three British executives fired from a Japanese company in London were victims of racial discrimination, an industrial tribunal ruled on Tuesday.

The tribunal said Quick Corporation, a Japanese financial information firm in London, had discriminated against and unfairly dismissed Clifford Wakeman and Stuart Mitchell, both white, and Ashok Solanki, who was of Asian origin.
The three men said British staff were paid less than Japanese employees and were prevented from advancing to the top levels of the company.
Wakeman claimed Noriaki Nakajima, the deputy managing director of Quick Corporation, had insulted and harassed him.

"After tossing aside a letter which Mr Wakeman had brought to his attention, Mr Nakajima said to him: "You have a strange skin colour and the shape of your head looks like a football'," the tribunal heard.
Although Nakajima denied the incident took place, the tribunal said he was a witness it could not rely on.

"We think that this outburst by Mr Nakajima revealed racist feelings towards Mr Wakeman, which motivated a course of conduct by Mr Nakajima against Mr Wakeman which was less favourable treatment on the grounds of Mr Wakeman's race. We refer to irritating restrictions and requirements imposed on Mr Wakeman," the tribunal said.
As only British employees were dismissed and without explanation, this constituted racial discrimination, it added.
The tribunal rejected the men's claim about discrimination because they were paid less than their Japanese co-workers.
Japanese employees were entitled to more money for the dislocation and disruption that was caused by their transfers, said the tribunal.
The three men, who were fired in 1994, had been earning between 40,000-50,000 pounds ($66,430-83,040).
Quick Corporation, which had earlier admitted to unfair dismissal but denied discrimination, will have to agree on compensation.

"Quick has examined all its employment policies and procedures in detail and continues to look at its responsibilities and obligations towards all its employees whatever their nationality to ensure that these are fulfilled and that they comply totally with UK employment law," the company said in a statement. ($1=.6021 Pound)
